top.title: Delta Killings: Police summon Omo-Agege, Egbo, others for questioning
top.description: *Thugs disrupted preparations, attacked Omo-Agege’s supporters, eyewitness insists By Clifford Ndujihe, Politics Editor The police yesterday summoned former Deputy Senate President, Senator Ovie Omo-Agege, Ughelli North Local Government Area Chairman, Jaro Egbo and others for questioning over the political violence that erupted during a campaign rally of the Nigeria Democratic Congress, NDC, in Uduere community, Ughelli North LGA of Delta State on Monday. The violence has triggered fresh accusations of political intimidation, police bias and inflammatory rhetoric ahead of the 2027 general elections. While the NDC yesterday boycotted a security meeting convened by the Inspector-General of Police, IGP, Olatunji Disu, accusing the police of failing to protect its members, the Peoples Democratic Party, PDP, called on President Bola Tinubu to renounce what it described as dangerous political rhetoric. On a day that supporters of the camps staged protest and counter protest over the killings in Ughelli, Delta State governor, Sheriff Oborevwori, who visited the troubled community, condemned the killings and directed security agencies to track down and arrest those responsible. The state government also imposed a dusk-to-dawn curfew across Ughelli North Local Government Area. The attack occurred on Monday during a political campaign event involving former deputy president of the Senate and NDC Delta Central senatorial candidate, Senator Ovie Omo-Agege. Four persons were confirmed dead, while the NDC said no fewer than 15 others were receiving treatment in intensive care. The Inspector-General of Police subsequently ordered an immediate, impartial and evidence-based investigation, including an examination of the circumstances surrounding the shooting and the conduct of police personnel deployed to the venue. However, Vanguard gathered that one of the four supporters of Omo-Agege, killed in the attack, identified as Efemena Umukoro, had his first child barely six months ago. Yesterday, conflicting casualty figures trailed the killings. with rival political camps claiming seven deaths, against six acknowledged by Governor Sheriff Oborevwori and the police. Ughelli North Chairman, Chief Jaro Egbo, who hails from Uduere, named three persons he said were killed on his side, including the community’s President-General, PG, Cosmos Ejovwoke. Former Deputy Senate President, Senator Ovie Omo-Agege, on the other hand, listed four members of his campaign organisation died. The competing accounts bring the number of claimed fatalities to seven, although the governor and police put the toll at six, pending investigations. This was as former Chief Justice of Nigeria, Justice Olukayode Ariwoola, retd., warned against a repeat of the deadly violence that followed the 2011 general elections, which claimed over 800 lives, urging political parties, security agencies and other stakeholders to take urgent steps to protect the 2027 electoral process. top.title: Depth Delivers: UTEP men win in Cancun without top scorers
top.description: The UTEP men's basketball team has raved about its depth early in the 2026-27 season. On their first long road trip of the year at the Cancun Challenge against the College of Charleston, they got to live it. Playing in Mexico without their two leading scorers, Cam McDaniels and Youssouf Traore, who did not make the trip because of injuries, UTEP overcame the challenge and the now-4-2 Cougars, 80-69. The 5-1 Miners did it with a revamped lineup and depth, led by the most likely player, point guard Leif Moeller, and normal reserve Reid Cason. With the win, UTEP will play Eastern Michigan on Wednesday, Nov. 25 at 6:30 p.m. MT. UTEP made this look fairly routine, taking control with a 12-2 run that helped stake the Miners to a 42-26 lead they saw home. In building the first-half lead that proved decisive, the Miners held Charleston to 19% shooting (1-of-14 from 3-point range) and held the Cougars without a field goal for the final 7:42 of the half. Charleston got going a bit in the second half, but UTEP had the margin it needed. UTEP was consistent offensively all game, finishing at 54% to Charleston’s 34%. The Miners didn’t blink down the stretch against the Cougars’ press to win their fifth consecutive game. As he was brought in to do, the sophomore Moeller was the glue with 14 points and 10 rebounds. Cason, getting his first start as a Miner, scored 12 points on 6-of-8 shooting and had six rebounds. Freshman Donovan Criss continued the impressive start to his UTEP career, scoring 13 points to go with three assists. UTEP won bench points 31-16 despite having two normal reserves, Cason and Jace Whiting, in the starting lineup. Where the Miners struggled was getting outscored at the free-throw line, as the Cougars were 29-of-37 to UTEP’s 15-of-20, as both Augusto Cassia and Cason fouled out as part of the Miners’ 27 fouls. The Miners won points off turnovers 18-11 despite giving the ball away 16 times to Charleston’s 14. Up next The Miners close the Cancun Challenge on Wednesday, Nov. 25 against either Eastern Michigan at 6:30 p.m. MT. It will be streamed on FloCollege and carried on 600 ESPN El Paso. top.title: South-East 400-km $100m gas pipeline, recipe for region’s industrial growth — SEDC
top.description: By Chinedu Adonu For decades, businesses and industries across Nigeria’s South-East region have depended on generators for their daily operations at a high cost. From the manufacturing clusters in Aba, Abia State, to the industrial workshops in Nnewi, Anambra State, the commercial centres of Onitsha, the business communities of Enugu and the productive enterprises of Imo and Ebonyi states, they all face the high cost and unreliability of electricity, forcing them to spend millions of naira to power their generators just to ensure that they remain in business. It has not been easy for a region whose economic strength is deeply rooted in entrepreneurship, manufacturing, commerce, and small-scale industries. Indeed, the energy challenge remains a major obstacle to industrial expansion as they spend huge resources powering their factories. All of them, including small businesses, struggle with rising operational costs. Will the proposed 400-kilometer South-East Gas Distribution Pipeline Project, with an initial investment budget of approximately $100 million, be a game changer for them? This initiative by the South-East Development Commission, SEDC, is planned to connect natural gas resources around the region to industrial and commercial centres across the five states in the region. It was unveiled at the South- East Gas Infrastructure Investment and Project Development Ceremony in Enugu on October 27, 2026. The initiative is a partnership between SEDC and GasSync Limited, NNPC Gas Marketing Limited and other stakeholders. President Bola Tinubu, represented at the ceremony by the Deputy Speaker of the House of Representatives, Rt., Hon. Benjamin Kalu, described the project as an important step towards addressing the infrastructure deficit which has constrained the productive capacity of the South-East region. “There is a sound familiar to every manufacturer in Aba, Nnewi, Onitsha, Enugu and across the South-East. It is the sound of a generator,” Tinubu noted, adding that the resilience of South-East entrepreneurs should no longer be an excuse for inadequate infrastructure. “Our manufacturers should not have to spend more on generating electricity than on expanding production. Our young entrepreneurs should not find that the greatest obstacle to their ambition is the cost of keeping their machines running,” he pointed out. According to the President, Nigeria’s natural gas resources should be measured not merely by what lies beneath the soil but by the factories they power, the jobs they create and the prosperity they bring. top.description: FORT MYERS, Florida − This gauntlet was always going to give us a true evaluation of Purdue basketball and DePaul supplied valid documentation the Boilermakers have work to do. By the time Purdue attempted its first shot, the Boilers already had three turnovers. "I feel like we played hard for 40 minutes, but just not smart for 40 minutes," Purdue guard Gicarri Harris said. Purdue's ability to adapt will need to come quick. Over the next three weeks, the Boilermakers will see two of the eight teams with a higher defensive KenPom rating than DePaul. Iowa State (second in KenPom adjusted defensive efficiency) on Dec. 5 and Tennessee (fifth) on Dec. 11. The tough lessons learned in Tuesday's bare knuckle brawl might be what a team with some young guards who'd never faced that level of physical play before needs to see. He's seen this story before and what his Blue Demons team was able to utilize against Purdue on Tuesday will benefit the Boilermakers long term, he believes. top.title: Gilbert Arenas reveals how James Harden's influence is bigger than most people realize
top.description: Gilbert Arenas reveals how James Harden's influence is bigger than most people realize originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Now that James Harden is on the Cleveland Cavaliers , it looks like he is in decline, even if he has some promising games here and there. This is natural, of course, given his age and the 2026-27 season being his 18th year in the NBA. However, this has led to some people disrespecting him and his place in the record books. In fact, Harden is more influential than some people expect in the modern NBA. Even multi-time All-Star Gilbert Arenas agrees with the sentiment that Harden is one of the most influential players in the modern age. It may sound wild to some people, but Arenas is making a valid point there. Gilbert Arenas argues in favor of James Harden's massive influence on the modern NBA Despite his impressive legacy, it seems that Harden is still one of the players who gets regularly ridiculed in NBA circles. Even former players take some jabs at Harden, especially because of his struggles during the Playoffs. He has had tremendous regular seasons, but he can't seem to figure it out in the postseason. Yes, he has struggled during the Playoffs, but that should not erase all of his contributions. Arenas is one of the people who have not overlooked how influential Harden has been to the game. Not only has he brought the step-back to become a weapon that every star player has nowadays, but he has had an influence on the rest of the league. MORE: A Cavaliers insider reveals the root of James Harden's problems before the 2026-27 season Many modern stars have followed Harden's example of being a bigger guard who dominates the usage. The likes of Luka Doncic and Cade Cunningham come to mind as players who fit the mold. At the same time, Harden is also influential with moves like the step-back and the ability to generate free throws with smart drives to the paint. "James doesn't get the credit for being as smart as he is. You're talking about a guy who studied the game to the point where he used the rule book to his advantage. We can say what we want, but this NBA is James Harden's NBA. The shooting part of it and the threes are Steph's, but the NBA itself, this has been James Harden's NBA," Arenas said on his Gil's Arena show about Harden's influence . Harden is still in the NBA today, doing a lot of things that made him such a fantastic player during his prime with the Houston Rockets or even during his days with the Brooklyn Nets and Philadelphia 76ers . There are still glimpses from time to time that remind people of what Arenas is pointing out about influence. top.title: Florida basketball center Rueben Chinyelu’s historic day vs. Milwaukee puts him in rare SEC territory
top.description: [Alan Youngblood/Gainesville Sun] Florida basketball center Rueben Chinyelu’s historic day vs. Milwaukee puts him in rare SEC territory appeared first on ClutchPoints . The No. 3 Florida Gators, who recently lost to the Houston Cougars , avoided getting upset by the Milwaukee Panthers on Tuesday at Tower Hill Arena in Gainesville, thanks in large part to the incredible night senior big man Rueben Chinyelu had. Chinyelu flexed his muscles and dominated the visiting Panthers, finishing with 25 points and 16 rebounds, while shooting 10-for-12 from the field, 1-for-1 from behind the arc and 4-for-4 from the free-throw line in 31 minutes of action. He added two blocks and an assist, as Florida basketball improved to 7-1 overall. With his stellar performance against Milwaukee, Chinyelu also put himself in an elite group of SEC players. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) “He’s just the second SEC player in 30 years with 25 PTS, 15 REB and 80% shooting in a game,” the official X (formerly Twitter) account of the SEC Network shared. It was quite a bounce-back showing from Chinyelu, who only appeared in 12 minutes in the previous Florida game against the West Virginia Mountaineers at home last Friday, scoring just two points with four rebounds and two assists before fouling out in an 85-72 victory. Chinyelu had actually produced minimally on offense in the three games before his eruption against Milwaukee, as he racked up just a total of 14 points on 5-for-11 shooting over that stretch. Chinyelu isn’t known for scoring as much as the toughness he brings inside and his ability to clean the glass for Florida , but it was great for the Gators to see him confidently get buckets on Tuesday. If anything, Chinyelu’s big night against the Panthers is a good momentum-builder for him as the Gators next take on the No. 16 Duke Blue Devils on Dec. 1 in Gainesville. top.title: Brian Kelly would be ‘surprised’ if SEC doesn’t give LSU the boot after RJ Luis controversy
top.description: Brian Kelly doesn’t see this ending well for LSU. SEC leadership is expecting to meet on Dec. 3, with the future of Kelly’s former employer up for debate . “This has gotten to the point where they will have a meeting on Dec. 3. The presidents will vote and I’ll actually be surprised if they don’t vote them out,” Kelly said in an appearance on SiriusXM’s “The Early Read” on Tuesday. Coach Brian Kelly of the LSU Tigers squats on the sideline during a 2025 game. Getty Images The Tigers have drawn the ire of their own conference in recent months by recruiting players who signed professional contracts for their football and basketball teams. Things came to a head when Will Wade’s men’s basketball team rostered and then played former St. John’s star RJ Luis in a game against UL Monroe on Nov. 18 — despite “numerous representations” that he wouldn’t take the court, according to the SEC. The following day, LSU president Wade Rousse told Wade not to play Luis , who spent time with the NBA’s Jazz and Celtics, but never got into any action. “They’ve asked them to come and meet them halfway a couple of times,” Kelly said. “I think the Luis situation and playing him in the game went against any kind of good faith that they had. I think this is going to go right down to a vote. College football and college athletics will all have to take notice with where we are and where we want to go.” Kelly, the Tigers’ former football coach, was famously fired eight games into his fourth season leading the team, with a 34-14 mark during his tenure. The move resulted in a $54 million payout and led to the hiring of Lane Kiffin — who opted not to put Dae’Quan Wright and Zxavian Harris on his roster this season despite speculation he’d find spots for the NFLers after they were granted an extra year of eligibility. The SEC officially passed a rule in August barring teams from rostering players who signed professional contracts in their respective sports, with commissioner Greg Sankey having authority to enforce penalties and sanctions. RJ Luis Jr. dribbles up court during LSU’s recent win over the ULM Warhawks. USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect “I don’t have any firsthand information other than following it like you folks have, and knowing Greg Sankey and what they’re about,” Kelly said. “They wanna be able to present the SEC rules and regulations relative to how member institutions operate on a day-to-day basis. That hasn’t been followed. I think that they’ve reached that point where, you know what? We can’t keep bluffing. We’ve gotta make a decision here, and I think we’re gonna have some kind of decision, whether it’s terminating their membership or whether people are suspended, the SEC’s gonna act.”

top.title: Pistons down Magic, Celtics hold off Wizards
top.description: Detroit's Daniss Jenkins and Ausar Thompson combine to block Orlando's Anthony Black (Rich Storry) The Detroit Pistons shrugged off the injury absence of Cade Cunningham to keep their NBA Cup hopes alive on Tuesday with a gritty 104-86 road victory over the Orlando Magic. Isaiah Joe led Detroit's scoring with 21 points after nailing five three-pointers as five Pistons players finished in double figures. Orlando, who could have booked their place in the knockout rounds with a victory, started brightly to take a 22-16 lead after the first quarter. But a devastating scoring burst from Detroit in the second quarter, outscoring Orlando 32-14, changed the contest. Detroit took a 48-36 lead into half-time and maintained a double-digit cushion for most of the remainder of the game. "I thought our defense was elite tonight," Pistons coach J.B. Bickerstaff said. "On a night where we were down some offense, we knew we were going to have to hang our hat on the defensive end of the floor and I love the way that everybody contributed. "Everbody bought into it and that was the best part. We knew it was going to be a gritty, physical game, but our guys did a great job." Orlando lead the Eastern Conference Group A with a 3-1 record while the Pistons are in third place on 2-1 behind the Toronto Raptors. The Boston Celtics all but locked up their place in the quarter-finals after holding off a furious rally from the Washington Wizards to score a 131-116 win on the road in the East's Group C. Jayson Tatum scored 41 points for the Celtics while Paul George added 28 and Neemias Queta 21 to halt Boston's four-game losing streak. The Celtics looked to be cruising towards a crushing win after racing into a 34-point lead just before half-time. But the Wizards hit back to outscore Boston 40-24 in the third quarter and got to within seven points of the lead late in the fourth at 119-112. Boston regrouped down the stretch and a pair of three-pointers from Baylor Scheierman saw the Celtics pull clear. "We had a tough week last week for various different reasons," Tatum said of Boston's run of four straight losses before Tuesday. "But you can't change what happens. We always try to focus on today," he told NBC. Tatum added he was not surprised by the Wizards' rally. "No lead is safe and they get paid to play basketball too, right?" he said. "They’ve got a lot of talent over there so it was just a case of trying to weather the storm." rcw/pst

top.title: Richard Sherman makes bold prediction for Sunday’s NFC West showdown
top.description: If anyone has an idea of what it’s like to play for the Seahawks and 49ers , it’s Richard Sherman. For the second time this season, the teams will clash, and Sherman was asked who he believes will win Sunday at Levi’s Stadium. 49ers quarterback Brock Purdy dropping back to pass in an NFL game against the Vikings. It’s too hard to bet against the San Francisco 49ers right now with how they’re rolling and how well they’re playing offensively and defensively.”… pic.twitter.com/990ppQwfl4 — Coach Yac (@Coach_Yac) November 25, 2026 “I think this is going to be a fantastic, fun game to watch,” Sherman said. “I just think it’s going to be too hard to bet against the San Francisco 49ers right now with how they’re rolling and how well they’re playing offensively and defensively.” The last time the teams met was in early October; they were nearly even until the fourth quarter, when San Francisco pulled ahead with a 7-yard touchdown pass from Brock Purdy to Brandin Cooks and followed it with a two-point conversion by Mike Evans to make the score, 29-26. Seattle kicked a field goal to tie the game, but the 49ers kicked a field goal on their ensuing possession and prevented Seattle from scoring on its final offensive drive — holding on for a 32-29 victory. “[Kyle Shanahan] is looking at that first game and watching things; he could’ve done better. That Brock could have done better. They could’ve called better in terms of offensive line and protections, to protect Brock better,” Sherman said. “I’m looking forward to seeing how it goes.” Purdy completed 19 of 29 passes for 189 yards, with two touchdowns, one interception and three sacks. One of the reasons Sherman believes San Francisco can win is if Purdy doesn’t turn the ball over. Purdy leads the NFL in quarterback rating (84.6) and has thrived protecting the football, having only five interceptions and a completion percentage of 71. top.title: Greenwich Bank opens Warri, Uyo branches, targets five more cities
top.description: By Peter Egwuatu Greenwich Bank Limited has opened branches in Warri, Delta State, and Uyo, Akwa Ibom State, as it targets five additional cities in its nationwide expansion drive. The new outlets bring its physical network to seven, following the opening of five branches in Lagos, Ondo and Ekiti states in October. The Bank plans to extend its operations to Asaba, Port Harcourt, Abuja, Benin and Ibadan in the coming months. Speaking at the commissioning of the Warri branch, Group Chairman of Greenwich Holdings, Kayode Falowo, described the Niger Delta as a strategic market, citing its economic importance and entrepreneurial potential, particularly in oil and gas, maritime services and logistics. He said: “Warri’s economic prospects extend beyond its natural resources to the entrepreneurs, traders, contractors, service providers and other businesses driving commercial activities in the region.” At the Uyo branch commissioning, Chairman of Greenwich Bank, Segun Oloketuyi, said the commercial banking licence would enable the institution to extend its 32 years of financial services experience to farmers, traders, civil servants, students and entrepreneurs. He identified credit facilities, agricultural and SME financing, trade and treasury services, salary solutions and digital banking as key offerings. Delta State Governor, Sheriff Oborevwori, represented by Commissioner for Finance, Fidelis Telije, urged residents, particularly small businesses, young entrepreneurs and women-owned enterprises, to take advantage of the Bank’s services. Similarly, Akwa Ibom State Governor, Umo Eno, represented by Commissioner for Finance, Emem Almond Bob, said the Uyo branch would improve access to banking services and credit, support business growth and potentially boost the state’s internally generated revenue. Managing Director of Greenwich Bank, Benson Ogundeji, said the branches would deepen customer engagement and bring financial solutions closer to businesses and individuals. He identified oil and gas, maritime services, agriculture, manufacturing, trade, logistics and SMEs as priority sectors, adding that the Bank would combine physical branches with technology-driven solutions to promote enterprise growth and financial inclusion. top.title: Political Violence: Dying for nothing as a Nigerian politician?
top.description: By Jide Ajani From the First Republic to the Fourth, politicians have been murdered, opposition figures silenced and political supporters killed. Yet, beyond the initial outrage, Nigeria has perfected the art of forgetting its dead. What, then, is the value of dying for a political cause in a country that cannot even preserve the memory of its political martyrs? The alleged assassination attempt on the former Deputy Senate President, Ovie Omo-Agege, two days ago, in Uduere community of Ughelli North LGA of Delta State, brings this odd reality into focus once again. Worse, many innocent, ordinary Nigerians have lost their lives while supporting or opposing politicians, only becoming part of an unidentified statistical figure. There is something inescapably tragic about dying while politicking in Nigeria. You could spend a lifetime building a political movement, challenging an unjust system, defending an electoral mandate, or fighting for an idea about your country’s future – or just being loud for nothing like a former, two-time state governor from the South West, or a former Rep and Senator from the North Central. You could become a household name, command enormous political influence and acquire a place in the nation’s history. Then, one morning, gunmen arrive, bullets are fired, and your life is terminated. There will be outrage. Condemnations will pour in. Politicians will issue statements, newspapers will publish editorials (like this), civil society organisations will demand justice, and the police will announce investigations. And then, Nigeria happens, and the people move on. The murder will become another entry in the country’s expanding archive of unresolved political crimes. The victim’s name will gradually disappear from public conversations, except when anniversary commemorations provide an opportunity for political speeches. Even the circumstances of the death may eventually become blurred by competing narratives, political expediency and the convenient amnesia of a nation. Is it, therefore, worth dying for Nigeria’s politics? The question intends to interrogate a society that celebrates political martyrs without demonstrating a corresponding commitment to preserving their legacies or establishing the truth about their deaths. On Monday, November 23, 2026, four persons were killed during an alleged assassination attempt on the former Deputy Senate President, Ovie Omo-Agege, two days ago, in Uduere Community of Ughelli North LGA of Delta State. Over a dozen were said to have been injured. Mind you, in an outburst of emotive frustration about happenings inthe political sphere, the self-same Omo-Agege had used the phrase ‘ ig and die’. He was to later clarify that he was merely drawing attention to the need for credible elections. top.title: FirstBank redefines personal lending experience with mApply, mServe
top.description: FirstBank has launched mApply and mServe, two digital solutions that are transforming how customers access and manage Personal Loan Against Salary (PLAS) facilities. The launch marks a significant milestone in FirstBank’s personal lending journey as, for the first time in the Bank’s history, eligible customers can initiate a personal loan application digitally without having to visit a branch to begin the process. Previously, accessing a PLAS facility required customers to engage the Bank through the branch or their Relationship Manager. With mApply, FirstBank has digitised the application journey, giving eligible customers the convenience of applying through the Bank’s digital channels from wherever they are. Through mApply, customers can initiate their PLAS application, provide the required document, select their employer and preferred branch for processing, and submit their request digitally. The solution significantly reduces the reliance on physical documentation and branch visits at the application stage, creating a simpler and more convenient route to accessing personal credit. PLAS is available to eligible salary account holders domiciled with FirstBank, as well as employees of eligible organisations seeking to move their salary accounts to the Bank. Customers can access up to N150 million, with repayment tenors of up to 72 months, subject to applicable terms and conditions. FirstBank is also extending the digital experience beyond loan application through mServe, its self-service solution for customers with existing PLAS facilities. With mServe, customers can view their loan details and outstanding balances, monitor their facilities and update relevant information, providing greater visibility and control over their loans without having to rely solely on branch-based servicing. Together, mApply and mServe create a more connected digital experience across the PLAS journey. While mApply simplifies how customers initiate and submit new loan requests, mServe provides existing borrowers with a convenient way to manage and monitor their facilities. Both solutions are accessible through FirstMobile and Lit App, bringing personal lending into the same digital environment customers already use for their everyday banking needs. top.title: NRS seeks simpler tax rules for creative sector
top.description: By Godwin Oritse The Nigeria Revenue Service (NRS) has called for simpler, clearer and business-friendly tax rules to unlock investment opportunities in Nigeria’s creative economy, stressing the need for a tax system that supports innovation, enterprise growth and wealth creation. The Service noted that the emergence of digital business models, intellectual property-driven enterprises and cross-border transactions required regulations that creators, entrepreneurs and investors could easily understand and navigate. Speaking at the just concluded high-level dialogue on taxation and investment in the creative economy during the Creative Africa Nexus (CANEX) event in Lagos, Executive Chairman of the NRS, Dr. Zacch Adedeji, described the creative economy as one of Nigeria’s most promising economic assets, noting that it had evolved beyond entertainment into a major source of employment, foreign exchange earnings, investment and economic opportunities. Adedeji who was represented by the Executive Director, People, Stakeholders and Communication, Mr. Obinna Ihedioha, also said that digital platforms had transformed how creative value was produced and commercialised, with entrepreneurs building businesses around copyrights, designs, brands and digital products. He reiterated that tax administration must evolve to accommodate these developments without discouraging innovation or business expansion. “The government needs sustainable revenue to invest in education, security, technology and infrastructure. But how we tax matters as much as what we collect. It shapes whether businesses start, whether investors come, and whether enterprises grow or stay small,” he said. Adedeji added that the new tax laws offered an opportunity to establish a more efficient system through clearer regulations, reduced compliance burdens for small businesses and improved taxpayer support. He identified clarity, understanding and value as essential to effective taxation, stressing that formalisation should provide creative businesses with tangible benefits, including access to finance, contracts, investment, wider markets and legal protection. The NRS, he said, participated in CANEX through a high-level dialogue, an Investment and Tax Advisory Hub for creators and investors, and the Creative Economy Tax and Investment Initiative (CETII), designed to sustain engagement beyond the event. top.description: Photo by Perry Knotts/Getty Images Aaron Rodgers has admitted the Pittsburgh Steelers need to get DK Metcalf more involved after the wide receiver endured another frustrating performance against the Philadelphia Eagles. His afternoon also ended in controversy after he was ejected following an altercation with Eagles cornerback Cooper DeJean. The 28-year-old has struggled to make an impact throughout the campaign, recording 36 catches for 434 yards and two touchdowns across 10 appearances. The Bank plans to extend its operations to Asaba, Port Harcourt, Abuja, Benin and Ibadan in the coming months. Speaking at the commissioning of the Warri branch, Group Chairman of Greenwich Holdings, Kayode Falowo, described the Niger Delta as a strategic market, citing its economic importance and entrepreneurial potential, particularly in oil and gas, maritime services and logistics. He said: “Warri’s economic prospects extend beyond its natural resources to the entrepreneurs, traders, contractors, service providers and other businesses driving commercial activities in the region.” At the Uyo branch commissioning, Chairman of Greenwich Bank, Segun Oloketuyi, said the commercial banking licence would enable the institution to extend its 32 years of financial services experience to farmers, traders, civil servants, students and entrepreneurs. He identified credit facilities, agricultural and SME financing, trade and treasury services, salary solutions and digital banking as key offerings. Delta State Governor, Sheriff Oborevwori, represented by Commissioner for Finance, Fidelis Telije, urged residents, particularly small businesses, young entrepreneurs and women-owned enterprises, to take advantage of the Bank’s services. Similarly, Akwa Ibom State Governor, Umo Eno, represented by Commissioner for Finance, Emem Almond Bob, said the Uyo branch would improve access to banking services and credit, support business growth and potentially boost the state’s internally generated revenue. Managing Director of Greenwich Bank, Benson Ogundeji, said the branches would deepen customer engagement and bring financial solutions closer to businesses and individuals. He identified oil and gas, maritime services, agriculture, manufacturing, trade, logistics and SMEs as priority sectors, adding that the Bank would combine physical branches with technology-driven solutions to promote enterprise growth and financial inclusion. Greenwich Holdings has over three decades of financial services experience, with interests in commercial banking, capital markets, asset management and securities. nigeria.title: Political Violence: Dying for nothing as a Nigerian politician?
nigeria.description: By Jide Ajani From the First Republic to the Fourth, politicians have been murdered, opposition figures silenced and political supporters killed. Yet, beyond the initial outrage, Nigeria has perfected the art of forgetting its dead. What, then, is the value of dying for a political cause in a country that cannot even preserve the memory of its political martyrs? The alleged assassination attempt on the former Deputy Senate President, Ovie Omo-Agege, two days ago, in Uduere community of Ughelli North LGA of Delta State, brings this odd reality into focus once again. Worse, many innocent, ordinary Nigerians have lost their lives while supporting or opposing politicians, only becoming part of an unidentified statistical figure. There is something inescapably tragic about dying while politicking in Nigeria. You could spend a lifetime building a political movement, challenging an unjust system, defending an electoral mandate, or fighting for an idea about your country’s future – or just being loud for nothing like a former, two-time state governor from the South West, or a former Rep and Senator from the North Central. You could become a household name, command enormous political influence and acquire a place in the nation’s history. Then, one morning, gunmen arrive, bullets are fired, and your life is terminated. There will be outrage. Condemnations will pour in. Politicians will issue statements, newspapers will publish editorials (like this), civil society organisations will demand justice, and the police will announce investigations. And then, Nigeria happens, and the people move on. The murder will become another entry in the country’s expanding archive of unresolved political crimes. The victim’s name will gradually disappear from public conversations, except when anniversary commemorations provide an opportunity for political speeches. Even the circumstances of the death may eventually become blurred by competing narratives, political expediency and the convenient amnesia of a nation. Is it, therefore, worth dying for Nigeria’s politics? The question intends to interrogate a society that celebrates political martyrs without demonstrating a corresponding commitment to preserving their legacies or establishing the truth about their deaths. On Monday, November 23, 2026, four persons were killed during an alleged assassination attempt on the former Deputy Senate President, Ovie Omo-Agege, two days ago, in Uduere Community of Ughelli North LGA of Delta State. Over a dozen were said to have been injured. Mind you, in an outburst of emotive frustration about happenings inthe political sphere, the self-same Omo-Agege had used the phrase ‘ ig and die’. He was to later clarify that he was merely drawing attention to the need for credible elections. nigeria.title: FirstBank redefines personal lending experience with mApply, mServe
nigeria.description: FirstBank has launched mApply and mServe, two digital solutions that are transforming how customers access and manage Personal Loan Against Salary (PLAS) facilities. The launch marks a significant milestone in FirstBank’s personal lending journey as, for the first time in the Bank’s history, eligible customers can initiate a personal loan application digitally without having to visit a branch to begin the process. Previously, accessing a PLAS facility required customers to engage the Bank through the branch or their Relationship Manager. With mApply, FirstBank has digitised the application journey, giving eligible customers the convenience of applying through the Bank’s digital channels from wherever they are. Through mApply, customers can initiate their PLAS application, provide the required document, select their employer and preferred branch for processing, and submit their request digitally. The solution significantly reduces the reliance on physical documentation and branch visits at the application stage, creating a simpler and more convenient route to accessing personal credit. PLAS is available to eligible salary account holders domiciled with FirstBank, as well as employees of eligible organisations seeking to move their salary accounts to the Bank. Customers can access up to N150 million, with repayment tenors of up to 72 months, subject to applicable terms and conditions. FirstBank is also extending the digital experience beyond loan application through mServe, its self-service solution for customers with existing PLAS facilities. With mServe, customers can view their loan details and outstanding balances, monitor their facilities and update relevant information, providing greater visibility and control over their loans without having to rely solely on branch-based servicing. Together, mApply and mServe create a more connected digital experience across the PLAS journey. While mApply simplifies how customers initiate and submit new loan requests, mServe provides existing borrowers with a convenient way to manage and monitor their facilities. Both solutions are accessible through FirstMobile and Lit App, bringing personal lending into the same digital environment customers already use for their everyday banking needs. nigeria.title: NRS seeks simpler tax rules for creative sector
nigeria.description: By Godwin Oritse The Nigeria Revenue Service (NRS) has called for simpler, clearer and business-friendly tax rules to unlock investment opportunities in Nigeria’s creative economy, stressing the need for a tax system that supports innovation, enterprise growth and wealth creation. The Service noted that the emergence of digital business models, intellectual property-driven enterprises and cross-border transactions required regulations that creators, entrepreneurs and investors could easily understand and navigate. Speaking at the just concluded high-level dialogue on taxation and investment in the creative economy during the Creative Africa Nexus (CANEX) event in Lagos, Executive Chairman of the NRS, Dr. Zacch Adedeji, described the creative economy as one of Nigeria’s most promising economic assets, noting that it had evolved beyond entertainment into a major source of employment, foreign exchange earnings, investment and economic opportunities. Adedeji who was represented by the Executive Director, People, Stakeholders and Communication, Mr. Obinna Ihedioha, also said that digital platforms had transformed how creative value was produced and commercialised, with entrepreneurs building businesses around copyrights, designs, brands and digital products. He reiterated that tax administration must evolve to accommodate these developments without discouraging innovation or business expansion. “The government needs sustainable revenue to invest in education, security, technology and infrastructure. But how we tax matters as much as what we collect. It shapes whether businesses start, whether investors come, and whether enterprises grow or stay small,” he said. Adedeji added that the new tax laws offered an opportunity to establish a more efficient system through clearer regulations, reduced compliance burdens for small businesses and improved taxpayer support. He identified clarity, understanding and value as essential to effective taxation, stressing that formalisation should provide creative businesses with tangible benefits, including access to finance, contracts, investment, wider markets and legal protection. The NRS, he said, participated in CANEX through a high-level dialogue, an Investment and Tax Advisory Hub for creators and investors, and the Creative Economy Tax and Investment Initiative (CETII), designed to sustain engagement beyond the event. nigeria.title: Edo Police parades security operative for allegedly leaking information to cultists
nigeria.description: By Ozioruva Aliu BENIN CITY — THE Edo State Police Command said four members of the Edo State Security Corps, ESSC, have been arrested for allegedly leaking information to suspected cultists to enable them evade arrests. The Command’s spokesperson, Eno Ikoedem, disclosed this while parading 16 suspects arrested across the state in connection with various criminal activities. The suspects, Isaac Irú we, Ashem Gideon, Tony Okhiale and Venture Uzu were arrested at Evbhomore community, in Ovia North-East Local Government Area of the state. They were accused of leaking information on police movements to cultists, enabling them to escape arrest. According to the Command, operatives of the Anti-Cultism Unit acted on intelligence on cult initiation activities in Benin City and immediately swung into action. “Upon getting there, we discovered that someone was giving out information on our movement to these cultists who escaped arrest. “Further investigation revealed that these men are members of the Edo State Security Corps, and four of them have been arrested and they are in our custody.” The command said investigation was still ongoing to ascertain their roles in the secret cult organisation. nigeria.title: Petrol imports crash 52% as crude, wheat top Lagos ports
nigeria.description: By Godwin Oritse Imports of Premium Motor Spirit (PMS), also known as petrol, through Lagos ports plunged by 52.23 per cent in November, while crude oil and bulk wheat ranked among the leading commodities imported through the ports in October and November. According to the Shipping Position document obtained from the Nigerian Ports Authority (NPA), PMS imports fell to 73,895 metric tonnes in November from 328,231 metric tonnes recorded in October. Crude oil imports through Lagos ports also dropped sharply, with 702,254 metric tonnes recorded in October, while no crude oil import was recorded in November. Bulk wheat ranked among the major commodities imported through Lagos ports during the period, with a combined 461,190 metric tonnes recorded in September, October and November. The breakdown showed that wheat imports rose to 252,348 metric tonnes in October and declined by 17.24 per cent to 208,842 metric tonnes in November. Other commodities on the import chart included 402,126 metric tonnes of PMS, 209,000 metric tonnes of Automotive Gas Oil (AGO), or diesel, 212,700 metric tonnes of bulk sugar, 150,000 metric tonnes of aviation fuel and 114,263 metric tonnes of bulk salt. Bulk sugar imports stood at 109,350 metric tonnes in October and 103,400 metric tonnes in November, while bulk salt imports rose from 33,000 metric tonnes to 81,263 metric tonnes over the same period. The document also showed that 624 trucks, 157 transformers and three Rubber-Tyred Gantry (RTG) cranes were received through Lagos ports during the period under review. nigeria.title: FCMB Group’s pretax profit rises 103% to N272.8bn in 9mths
nigeria.description: FCMB Group Plc reported pretax profit of N272.8 billion for the nine months ended September 30, up 103% from N134.5 billion a year earlier, driven by improved interest margins and a lower cost-to-income ratio. Annualised return on average equity rose to 30.1% from 22.4% a year earlier, while annualised return on average assets rose to 3.9% from 2.3%. Gross earnings for the same nine-month period rose 21% from a year earlier to N1 trillion, while after-tax profit increased 85.7% to N232.9 billion from N125.5 billion. Annualised earnings per share rose to N4.59, up 15% from N3.99 for full-year 2025, despite the expanded share base post-recapitalisation. The group’s unaudited results include the audited results of its Nigerian banking subsidiary – First City Monument Bank Limited. Commenting, FCMB Group’s Chief Executive Officer, Mr. Ladi Balogun, said he expects fourth-quarter earnings to benefit from a seasonal increase in digital lending and payments and lower operating expenses after the group recognised the full 2026 Asset Management Corporation of Nigeria levy in the first nine months. “With nine-month RoE at 30%, we expect full-year RoE to be materially above an earlier guidance of 25%, providing a strong foundation for further profitable growth and sustained shareholder value creation,” Balogun said. FCMB Group’s interest income rose 23.4%, while interest expense fell 3% as low-cost deposits made up a larger share of customer deposits. Net interest income rose 52.3% to N534.2 billion from N350.8 billion a year earlier, and net interest margin rose to 12.3% from 10.1%. Operating expenses rose 12.5% to N268.9 billion from N239 billion a year earlier, while the cost-to-income ratio fell to 43.5% from 55.5%. nigeria.title: Osun man tortures 21-yr-old son to death over N75,000, phone
nigeria.description: By Shina Abubakar Osogbo —The Osun State Police Command has said it arrested a 48-year-old man, Ogunniran Kayode over alleged murder of his son, Raphael, at Faaji, Odo-Otin Local Government Area of the state. A statement by the command’s Public Relations Officer, Abiodun Ojelabi, yesterday, stated that the police received intelligence on October 19, 2026, that the suspect tortured his 21-year-old son to death. Then he buried his body in a shallow grave. Following the intel, the statement disclosed that the operatives of the command swung into action and arrested the suspect as he confessed to the killing of his son. “During the interrogation, he stated that his son stole a sum of N75,000 and absconded with one android phone he bought for him on easy buy to an unknown place. “And being a member of Iru-Ekun Security Network, he was able to get the son arrested through the help of his colleague.” “The case was then transferred to Homicide Section for further investigation”, the statement added. Meanwhile, operatives of the homicide unit visisted the crime scene and the shallow grave, where details and pictorial evidence of the torture were retrieved. The state Police Commissioner, Ibrahim Zungura, therefore, warned individuals with criminal intent to desist from the act or face full wrath of the law. nigeria.title: No missing funds in $2.04bn Duke Oil crude cargoes — NNPC
nigeria.description: By Obas Esiedesa, Abuja The Nigerian National Petroleum Company Limited (NNPC) has dismissed reports alleging that $2.04 billion realised from crude oil cargoes lifted by Duke Oil Company Incorporated, now NNPC Trading S.A., was unaccounted for, insisting that all transactions were fully reconciled. The company said the $2.04 billion represented the gross value of 29 cargoes whose proceeds were set off against the cost of refined petroleum products supplied to Nigeria under the Direct Sale Direct Purchase (DSDP) programme. In a statement by its Chief Corporate Communications Officer, Andy Odeh, NNPC said the absence of separate dollar receipts for some cargoes did not indicate missing funds. “No separate receipt appears because the crude sale proceeds were set off against the product purchase price, as the contracts provide,” it stated. Under the DSDP programme, participating traders lifted crude oil in exchange for refined petroleum products, including petrol, for the Nigerian market. NNPC explained that while crude was priced in dollars, products supplied were sold in naira, with transactions reconciled and captured in the audited financial statements of the relevant entities. The company said all 59 cargoes referenced in the reports were accounted for, adding that 30 were paid for in dollars, while proceeds from 28 cargoes, valued at approximately $1.96 billion, were remitted in naira to the NNPC Group Treasury or NNPC Upstream Investment Management Services accounts. The remaining cargo, a February 2023 Bonga tax-oil lifting valued at about $75.9 million, was paid into the then designated Federal Inland Revenue Service dollar account. On Duke Oil’s ownership, NNPC said it was incorporated in 1989 as its wholly owned trading subsidiary, adding that the relationship was documented in its corporate history, audited financial statements and NEITI’s 2023 industry report. It maintained that transactions between the company and its subsidiaries were disclosed as related-party transactions under International Financial Reporting Standards. NNPC reaffirmed its commitment to transparency and accountability, but warned that it reserved the right to take legal action against publications it considered false or misleading. nigeria.title: CBN holds MPR at 23%, says external reserves drop temporary
nigeria.description: By Emma Ujah, Abuja Bureau Chief The Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) has retained its Monetary Policy Rate (MPR) at 23 per cent, dismissing concerns over a decline of over $300 million in external reserves as a temporary, seasonal movement. Governor of the CBN, Mr. Olayemi Cardoso, disclosed this yesterday at a press conference announcing the outcome of the 308th meeting of the Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) in Abuja. The bank also retained the standing facilities corridor at +50/-300 basis points around the MPR, Cash Reserve Requirement (CRR) for Deposit Money Banks at 45 per cent, Merchant Banks at 16 per cent and Non-TSA public sector deposits at 75 per cent. Explaining the decision to retain the policy rate, Cardoso said: “In reaching its decision, the committee acknowledged the continued decline in headline inflation, but remained mindful of lingering upside risks, particularly those arising from the ongoing Middle East conflict, which could sustain pressure on energy prices. “In addition, the MPC observed that the anticipated increase in spending from the end-of-year festive season and election-related activities could impact aggregate demand with likely upward pressure on prices. “Nevertheless, the committee judged that maintaining the current policy stance is appropriate to safeguard the gains of disinflation so far achieved, while remaining data-dependent and vigilant in taking further appropriate measures.” He added that continued exchange rate stability and improved food supply associated with the harvest season would further strengthen the disinflation process. Cardoso said headline inflation had moderated for five consecutive months, reflecting sustained exchange rate stability and improved monetary policy transmission. “However, given the prevailing headwinds, which have slowed the pace of moderation in price pressures, members were of the view that maintaining the current policy stance would further anchor inflation expectations and support the disinflation process,” he said. On concerns over the decline in external reserves by over $300 million, Cardoso said the movement was not a source of worry, describing it as seasonal. “Our reserves is in a very strong position. So, that, I want to say, has not changed. And in actual fact, I believe it will continue to improve. What you mention is something that is transient,” he said. He explained that portfolio investors tend to recalibrate their positions towards year-end, while domestic users also increase demand for foreign exchange to hedge against future uncertainties. “These are all seasonal issues. And of course, with the elections coming, there’s more spending that is going on. These are all seasonal. And we believe very strongly that as we go into the next year, we will find a major moderation in the volatility that you have seen,” he said. nigeria.title: Tears as victims of Bayelsa boat mishap get mass burial
nigeria.description: By Emem Idio YENAGOA — It was tears and wailing at the Azikoro Cemetery in Yenagoa, Bayelsa State, yesterday, as victims of Friday’s boat mishap in Southern Ijaw Local Government Area of the state, were laid to rest in a mass burial. The burial, which commenced at about 11am, ended at 4pm, when the last batch of bodies, wrapped in black plastic bags, were brought to the cemetery in ambulances. The exercise was supervised by the Secretary to the State Government, Prof. Nimibofa Ayawei, and the Commissioner for Environment, Mr. Ebi Ololo, alongside other government officials. The cemetery was enveloped by a foul stench from the bodies, some of which had begun to decompose, as grieving relatives, friends and sympathisers gathered to witness the burial. Many mourners broke down in tears, while others stood in groups, speaking in hushed tones as the remains of their loved ones were lowered into shallow graves. One of the bereaved relatives, Timipreye Diepreye, who said she lost seven family members in the tragedy, faulted the manner in which relatives were informed about the mass burial. She said the family would have made arrangements for coffins for their deceased relatives, particularly those whose bodies were recovered on Friday, if they had been adequately informed ahead of the exercise. Also speaking, the Chairman of the Community Development Committee, CDC, of Ukubie community, Mr. Ruben Kemelate, said the tragedy had plunged the entire community into mourning, with hardly any family left untouched by the loss. Kemelate, who disclosed that his elder sister also died at the Federal Medical Centre, said the scale of the tragedy had left the community devastated. He said: “We are in a very sad mood. Every family is affected. There is no family that is not affected. Like me particularly, my elder sister died in the FMC. So, every family is in a sad mood. We are in a very sad mood as a community. “So far so good, we have recovered 35 bodies and we have buried 29. We buried one on the first day, one seven-year-old boy. nigeria.title: Campaign Violence: INEC awaits police case files to prosecute offenders
nigeria.description: By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA — The Independent National Electoral Commission, INEC, has asked the Nigeria Police Force to speed up the arrest, investigation and transmission of case files against perpetrators of campaign violence, so the Commission can prosecute them directly. The INEC Chairman, Professor Joash Amupitan, SAN, said swift action was necessary so that “impunity is decisively checked before January.” He spoke on Tuesday in Abuja at the Inspector General of Police’s Interactive Session with Chairmen and Secretaries of Political Parties on a peaceful electoral process before, during and after the 2027 General Elections. The session held at the Goodluck Ebele Jonathan Peace Conference Hall, Force Headquarters. According to a statement by the commission, last night, Amupitan said INEC was “deeply concerned by isolated incidents of campaign violence, intimidation, and attacks on political rivals, journalists, and electoral facilities.” No election, office, or partisan interest is worth the loss of a single Nigerian life. Achieving a peaceful political environment is a collective national responsibility, not the duty of a single institution”, he added. He said the Electoral Act 2026 had “significantly strengthened legal deterrence,” adding that Sections 96 and 97 prohibit inciting campaign rhetoric and ban the use of thugs, private armed guards or masquerades at political rallies. According to him, the Act prescribes penalties of up to ₦5 million or twelve months’ imprisonment for individuals, and up to ₦10 million for political parties, on initial breaches. “Under Section 148, INEC is empowered to prosecute electoral offenders directly upon receipt of completed case files,” he said, explaining the Commission’s request for prompt transmission of the files by the Police. The INEC chairman stressed that the Commission remained distinct from security agencies. “INEC is not a security agency; it lacks both the constitutional mandate and operational capacity to maintain public order, arrest offenders, or provide armed security,” he said. He said Section 95 of the Electoral Act assigns the duty of securing political rallies to the Police. The Section also mandates the Commissioner of Police in each state and the Federal Capital Territory (FCT) to provide adequate security for rallies and processions, with support from the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps, NSCDC, and other federal security agencies. nigeria.title: South-East governors working for my re-election — Tinubu
nigeria.description: By Johnbosco Agbakwuru ABUJA — AHEAD of the January 16 presidential election, President Bola Tinubu, on Monday, told the Igbo community and their leaders, in Lagos, that all the South-East governors are with him on the journey to make Nigeria a better place and are working for his re-election. The President said he was excited and that he would go home happy and eat because of their endorsement of his second term. He assured them of his administration’s commitment to inclusive governance, national unity and equity for all Nigerians. nigeria.title: Bellingham beauty in Real Madrid win; Arsenal, Man City held in Champions League
nigeria.description: Jude Bellingham scored one of the goals of the season as Real Madrid hammered PSV Eindhoven 5-1 on Tuesday to maintain their perfect record in this season’s Champions League, while Arsenal and Manchester City were both held to draws at home. Elsewhere, debutants Como and Real Betis continued their excellent form since the start of the league phase, but Aston Villa slumped to another defeat on their travels. Record 15-time European champions Real had to come from behind to beat PSV at the Bernabeu as they made it five wins from five in this season’s league phase to go clear at the top of the standings with 15 points. Dutch champions PSV led at half-time courtesy of an Ivan Perisic penalty, but Federico Valverde equalised five minutes after the restart. Bellingham then put Real ahead on the hour with a remarkable strike, as he controlled a Kylian Mbappe lay-off outside the box and then teed himself up for a sweet volley on the outside of his right boot which flew into the corner of the net. Vinicius Junior sealed the win for Jose Mourinho’s side, who have now claimed 10 consecutive victories in all competitions. “That one was a nice one, it popped up for me nicely and then I just hit it. I thought I would go with the outside of the boot a little bit, stab it a little bit, I am not one for smashing the ball too hard. It was a nice moment,” England star Bellingham told British broadcaster TNT Sports about his goal. nigeria.title: Bakassi Port, border reforms to unlock Cross River’s economic potential – Customs boss
nigeria.description: By Godwin Oritse The Comptroller-General of Customs, Bashir Adewale Adeniyi, has said the proposed Bakassi Deep Sea Port and planned modernisation of strategic border corridors will unlock Cross River State’s economic potential, boost regional commerce and reposition the state as a major gateway for international trade. Adeniyi, who spoke at the 6th AfSNET Investment Conference 2026 in Calabar, Cross River State, said the state was on the path to reclaiming its historic position as one of Nigeria’s foremost commercial hubs. He described the groundbreaking ceremony for the proposed Bakassi Deep Sea Port as a significant milestone that could transform the economic fortunes of Cross River State and strengthen its participation in international trade. Reflecting on Calabar’s commercial heritage, the Customs boss recalled that the city once hosted Nigeria’s busiest Customs port, noting that its trading history dated back approximately a century. He also highlighted that Nigeria’s first indigenous and longest-serving Comptroller-General of Customs hailed from Calabar, underscoring the state’s historic contribution to the Service and the country’s commercial development. Held under the theme “Celebrating Partnerships, Rewarding Excellence,” the event brought together company leadership and long-standing partners from Northern, Eastern and Western Nigeria. It paid tribute to the distributors who built markets and the dealers who remained committed through shifting economic conditions. Their enterprise and confidence have carried CFM’s products to customers and communities across the country. The highlight of the evening was the rewarding of CFM’s best-performing dealers across three categories: Trailblazer, Sterling and Titan. Winners received 5-tonne, 10-tonne and 15-tonne trucks, as well as baking ovens. The night closed with the presentation of a 45-tonne truck to the overall best-performing dealer. Nitin Mehta, Business Head, Wheat Milling & Pasta Business, Olam Agri, said the milestone reflects far more than time. “Fifteen years of growing together represents relationships built on trust, shared ambition and resilience. entertainment.description: Mentors, mentees, professionals and members of the public gathered at Eko Atlantic, Lagos, on Saturday, November 14, 2026, for the annual Women in Successful Careers (WISCAR) Mentoring Walk . Led by WISCAR Founder and Chairperson, Amina Oyagbola , the walk forms part of the lead-up to the organisation’s 18th Annual Leadership and Mentoring Conference. Participants were paired up for the walk along the Eko Atlantic, each with someone they had not met before. At the end of the route, they switched to new mentor-mentee partners for a short mentoring session, which gave everyone two fresh conversations in one morning. Back at the meeting point, participants shared what they had learnt from their partners, from career advice to personal lessons. entertainment.title: How Williams Alamu Graduated with First-Class Honours in Statistics from the University of Ibadan
entertainment.description: Williams Alamu marks his B.Sc. First-Class Honours graduation in Statistics from the University of Ibadan. There was a time when Williams Alamu would rather not sit an examination than risk getting a grade he wasn’t happy with. A B or a C in his Cambridge A-levels felt like a possibility he wasn’t ready to entertain, so he didn’t write the exams. A few years later, at 23, he has graduated from the University of Ibadan with a B.Sc. in Statistics, First-Class Honours and a CGPA of 3.65/4.0. Somewhere along the way, he decided that fear was no longer going to make his decisions for him. When Williams got into UI, he had a rather ambitious plan: become the Best Graduating Student in his faculty. Getting there would require more than good intentions. There were 5:30am wake-ups, difficult Statistics courses, friends who became unofficial tutors, a ChatGPT Pro subscription in 300 level, job offers he turned down and one Demography exam that kept him awake for 36 hours. University, as it turns out, came with quite a few plot twists. In this interview with BellaNaija, Williams takes us through the habits, people and decisions that shaped his academic journey. He also tells us whether he got that coveted top spot, what he learnt from the opportunities he put on hold, and what he would tell another student hoping to graduate with First-Class Honours. If that’s a goal you’re working towards, you may want to take notes. Literally or otherwise. Williams Alamu celebrates graduating with First-Class Honours in Statistics from the University of Ibadan. At what point did you realise you were chasing a record-breaking grade? Was it a goal from Day 1, or did it evolve? It was a goal from day one, actually. When I gained admission into the University of Ibadan, I already had my mind set on graduating as the Best Graduating Student in my faculty. I knew becoming the overall Best Graduating Student in the university would require an extraordinary amount of work, but I felt being the best in my faculty was something I wanted to work towards. And, of course, that would also mean graduating as the best student in my department. The motivation behind that goal goes back to shortly after secondary school, when my parents enrolled me in a Cambridge A-level programme. I went into it hoping to achieve three A-stars, but Chemistry was a major struggle. As the examinations approached, I became increasingly worried about my performance. I think I was more afraid of not meeting my own expectations than I was of the examination itself. The thought of getting a B or C frightened me so much that I eventually decided not to sit for the examinations. entertainment.title: Solape Fayemi Launches Saina Properties Across Four Markets
entertainment.description: For many people, buying property is one of the biggest financial decisions they will ever make. Yet, knowing who to trust, how to verify ownership and whether a property is worth the investment can make the process overwhelming. It is a challenge Solape Fayemi hopes to address with the launch of Saina Properties , a real estate company now operating across Nigeria, the United Kingdom, the United States and the United Arab Emirates. Officially unveiled at an event held on 17 November at the Marriott Hotel, Ikeja GRA, Lagos, Saina Properties is built around a simple idea: property ownership should be guided by sound advice, proper verification and professional support, not just the excitement of closing a deal. For Solape, whose experience in the investment industry shaped her understanding of money, risk and wealth creation, the decision to establish the company came from recognising the need for a more considered approach to real estate. “We are not building Saina Properties because the world needs another company selling properties. We are building Saina because we believe there is room for a different kind of real estate experience. One where advice comes before the transaction, where due diligence is not treated as an inconvenience, and where people are encouraged to ask questions, understand their options and make informed decisions,” she said at the launch. That philosophy is reflected in the company’s three core areas of expertise: Advisory & Verification, Sales & Brokerage, and Developments . Rather than focusing solely on connecting buyers to properties, Saina brings together the guidance investors need to assess opportunities, the support required to navigate property transactions, and involvement in real estate development. The company is also building on experience gained before its official launch, having supported more than 25 clients with property opportunities across different markets. An important part of its proposition is the role of professional expertise in protecting property investors. Fayemi’s position raises a familiar question: people consult doctors for medical concerns and lawyers for legal matters, so why do some investors leave significant property decisions in the hands of relatives simply because they are available or familiar with the location? While trust and family relationships matter, they do not automatically translate into the technical knowledge needed to assess a property, verify its documentation or understand its investment potential. These decisions require proper checks, market understanding and accountability. With its operations spanning four markets, Saina Properties aims to support individuals and investors looking to navigate property ownership with greater clarity, whether they are buying, selling or exploring development opportunities. I’m a physiotherapist, a strategy consultant, a healthcare entrepreneur, and I recently graduated from the University of Oxford with a distinction in Health Service Improvement and Evaluation. I have probably said that last part a hundred times since getting my results, and honestly, I don’t think I’m tired of saying it yet. Haha! One thing about me is that I like to be involved. I am sometimes curious about things that have absolutely nothing to do with what I’m supposed to be doing, and I genuinely enjoy working with people. I like organising things, bringing people together, and seeing an idea move forward to get accomplished. So I have known that going to Oxford was never going to be just about getting a master’s degree. Let me explain how I ended up there. I studied Physiotherapy at the University of Ibadan, where I graduated with First-Class Honours. During my undergraduate years, I was involved in quite a lot outside academics: student leadership, journalism, research, community health programmes and advocacy. My involvement in community health exposed me to how differently people experience healthcare depending on where they live, what they can afford and what information they have access to. I loved being a physiotherapist, and that allowed me to interrogate questions that went beyond individual patient care. Why do some people receive good healthcare while others struggle to access even basic services? How do we make healthcare more affordable? What role can technology play? And why do some seemingly good healthcare programmes struggle to produce lasting change? Eventually, I realised I wanted to study and work in a field that constantly seeks to improve health systems. entertainment.description: Have you ever spent six hours in an airport waiting for your connecting flight, watching the departure screens, browsing duty-free shops and wondering what the city outside looks like? Perhaps you were connecting through Istanbul, Doha, Dubai or Addis Ababa. You were technically in another country, but the closest you came to experiencing it was buying a souvenir at the airport. What if I told you that some airlines could help you turn that connection into an additional holiday, sometimes even providing accommodation? Having travelled to more than 70 countries, I have learnt that one of the smartest ways to travel is to pay attention to the journey, not just the destination. Many Nigerians book international tickets based on price, travel time and baggage allowance. These are important considerations, but there is another question worth asking: What else can this ticket give me? I am talking about stopovers, not the hurried two-hour connection where you are running between terminals, but an intentional break in your journey that allows you to experience another destination before continuing to the country you originally planned to visit. And with the right airline, itinerary and travel documents, that additional experience might cost less than you imagine. First, Understand What You Are Booking A layover is generally a connection between flights; a stopover is a longer, planned break in your journey. Airlines define these differently, and the distinction matters because some offer special hotel packages, sightseeing tours or complimentary accommodation to qualifying passengers. For example, imagine travelling from Lagos to London through Istanbul. Instead of spending a few hours at Istanbul Airport, you could investigate whether your ticket qualifies for a longer stopover, allowing you to explore Istanbul before continuing to London. You have now turned one international journey into an opportunity to experience two destinations outside Nigeria. The secret is to investigate the stopover before purchasing your ticket, rather than arriving at the airport and hoping the airline will allow you to stay longer. For visa purposes, Nigerians do not qualify, but with a valid Turkish visa you would be able to qualify for some of the perks. entertainment.title: Asali Africa: Serves Up ‘There’s Rice at Home’ A New Cooking Series Hosted by Chef Soliat Bada
entertainment.description: Chef Soliat Bada Anyone who grew up in a Nigerian home knows the line. You suggest buying food outside, and before you finish the sentence, someone reminds you that there’s rice at home. It is usually the end of the conversation. In Asali Africa’s new series, it is where the conversation starts. There’s Rice at Home is a cooking and conversation show from Asali Africa, the Lagos-based creative development agency, hosted by Chef Soliat Bada . In each episode, Soliat cooks one rice dish with a guest, and while the pot does its work, the two get into the kind of talk that usually happens around food: family, money and what success really looks like. Rice is the most ordinary thing in a Nigerian kitchen, and the show makes a good case that it doesn’t have to taste ordinary. Over five episodes, released every two weeks, the menu travels from Jamaica to Saudi Arabia, back home to Nigeria and on to Louisiana. You don’t just watch the food get made, either. The recipes are written up in full on Asali Africa’s website, with the ingredients and method laid out step by step, so you can watch Soliat cook a dish and then make it in your own kitchen. The season opens with Rice and Peas with Oxtail, the Jamaican Sunday staple of rice cooked in coconut milk with red kidney beans (the “peas”), served beside rich, slow-cooked oxtail. Soliat’s guest is Michael Famoroti , co-founder of Stears, and their conversation turns to family and black tax: the expectation that once you start earning, you start supporting the people who raised you. entertainment.title: Beyond the Mini LED Label: What Should Define Good Mini LED Performance?
entertainment.description: The presence of Mini LED tells a shopper something important about the light source behind an LCD panel. It does not, by itself, explain how that light is arranged, divided or controlled. Those implementation choices can have a major influence on contrast, black level performance, highlight control and the visibility of blooming in difficult scenes. From Presence To Performance That distinction matters because a category becomes more useful to consumers when it can be evaluated through clear performance principles rather than through a technology name alone. For Mini LED, three factors provide a practical starting point. The first is hardware local dimming. In a hardware based system, physical groups of LEDs can be brightened, dimmed or switched off independently across different areas of the screen. This gives the television more direct control over how light is distributed within a single image. The second is local dimming zone count and precision. A higher number of independently controlled zones can allow the backlight to respond in smaller areas, which can improve separation between bright highlights and surrounding dark regions when other major conditions are comparable. The number itself is not the whole story, but it is a useful indicator of how granular the backlight system can be. The third is backlight architecture. Full Array Local Dimming places controllable zones across the area behind the panel, providing the physical foundation for more localized light management than designs that illuminate the panel from the edges or operate the backlight more uniformly. Together, these three elements move the Mini LED conversation from a simple question of whether the technology is present to a more useful question: how effectively is the light being controlled? Where TCL Enters The Category Conversation TCL is relevant to that discussion because Mini LED has become a significant part of its global television business. According to Omdia data cited in TCL Electronics interim results, TCL ranked No. 1 globally by Mini LED TV shipment volume in the first half of 2026. TCL reported 2.43 million Mini LED TV shipments during the period, representing 77.1% year on year growth. That position follows a strong 2025, when TCL reported, based on Omdia data, a 31.1% share of global Mini LED TV shipments and 118.0% year on year shipment growth. Market scale does not, on its own, define technology leadership. What it does provide is evidence that a manufacturer has become an important participant in how the category develops. entertainment.description: “Men are not wired to show emotions.” A male friend once said to me during an argument. He was so convinced that I wondered whether a manual somewhere explained how men were manufactured. According to him, men were created to be strong, endure pain and keep their emotions to themselves. That was simply how they were made. “So, because you’re a man, you’re not supposed to feel hurt, fear or disappointment?” I disagreed. He insisted that showing emotions was not in a man’s nature. Who made that rule? Who decided that men could experience pain but must never be seen expressing it? At what point did being a man become synonymous with pretending that everything was fine? The conversation wilted, but it has stayed with me, perhaps because my friend wasn’t expressing an unusual opinion. He was repeating a stereotype many of us have heard all our lives: “Boys don’t cry.” “Be a man.” “Man up.” Three little expressions, and somewhere between being told to be strong and learning to say “I’m fine,” I wonder how many men have forgotten what it feels like to be heard. Frequent questions men are asked: “How far? Work nko?” “When are you getting married?” “Have you bought land?” “How is the family?” And the famous Nigerian question that can make an unemployed graduate dread family gatherings: “So, what are you doing now?” We often inquire about their achievements, responsibilities, and plans. These aspects are important, but how often do we ask about their fears? A father who leaves home before sunrise and returns exhausted, burdened by the weight of school fees, rent, and family expectations. A young graduate who has submitted countless job applications, yet still smiles politely when another relative inquires why he hasn’t found a job. A successful professional whose LinkedIn profile showcases numerous achievements, while his personal life tells a story that no one has thought to ask about. We admire their strength, we applaud their sacrifices, and we celebrate their accomplishments. But what about what they are going through? The person everyone leans on also needs somewhere to lean. Society has an interesting checklist for measuring a man’s success. A good job, a house, a car, a wife, children and financial stability. Preferably, all achieved before a certain age.
